key_insight: Fréchet Distance can be optimized as a practical training objective by computing it in a learned representation space while decoupling the large sample pool needed for a stable FD estimate from the small mini-batches used for gradient updates. This “FD-loss” (Representation Fréchet Loss) enables effective post-training improvements to visual generators.
problem_solved: Makes Fréchet Distance (long thought impractical as a loss) usable for training/guiding generative models by addressing sample-size vs. batch-size limitations in FD estimation.
method: Compute Fréchet Distance in a learned representation space (e.g., pretrained perceptual embeddings) rather than pixels.
Decouple FD estimation population size from gradient batch size — use a large feature pool (e.g., tens of thousands) to estimate moments and small mini-batches (e.g., ~1k) for gradient computation.
Post-train an existing base generator with the FD-loss in different representation spaces to consistently improve visual quality.
impact: Enables practitioners to use Fréchet-based objectives reliably and scalably to improve generative model quality with a lightweight post-training step; compatible with a variety of representation backbones and training pipelines.
visual_elements: Schematic: two-stream diagram showing a large feature pool for FD estimation (50k) vs. small mini-batch for gradients (1k) with arrows to FD-loss computation and backprop.
Before/After image grid: sample outputs from a base generator vs. after FD-loss post-training to highlight visual quality gains.
Bar/line chart: metric improvements (e.g., FID or similar) across representation spaces or datasets showing consistent gains.
Icon set: representation space examples (Inception / CLIP / SSL) with labels indicating where FD is computed.
paper_title: Representation Fréchet Loss for Visual Generation
paper_authors: Jiawei Yang, Zhengyang Geng, Xuan Ju, Yonglong Tian, Yue Wang
